merger_name: Respect Group – McLean Care residential aged care homes and independent living units
merger_description:
Respect Group Limited (**Respect Group**) is a not-for-profit registered charity and unlisted public company based in Tasmania, which provides residential aged care, retirement living, and support at home services focused on dignity and wellbeing for older adults. Respect Group owns and operates 41 residential aged care homes across Tasmania, New South Wales, Victoria, Western Australia, Queensland, and South Australia.

McLean Care Ltd (**McLean Care**) is a not-for-profit company limited by guarantee, based in Inverell, New South Wales, providing regional residential aged care and independent living units. McLean Care operates 6 residential aged care facilities in Inverell, Guyra, and Gunnedah in northern New South Wales, and Oakey and Millmerran in southern Queensland. It also operates co-located independent living units in Inverell and Gunnedah.

Respect Group proposes to acquire 100% of the business and assets owned by McLean Care through a two-step process in which the parties enter into an Implementation Deed, which implements a change of control of McLean Care whereby the directors of Respect Group are appointed to the board of McLean Care, such that McLean Care becomes an associated entity of Respect Group, and subsequently, the business and assets (including land) of McLean Care are transferred to Respect Group pursuant to a Deed of Gift.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Respect Group Limited (Respect Group) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of the business
and assets of McLean Care Ltd (McLean Care), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Respect Group, is a not-for-profit registered charity and
unlisted public company based in Tasmania, which provides
residential aged care, retirement living, and support at home services
focused on dignity and wellbeing for older adults. Respect Group
owns and operates 41 residential aged care homes across
Tasmania, New South Wales, Victoria, Western Australia,
Queensland, and South Australia.
The target, McLean Care, is a not-for-profit company limited by
guarantee, based in Inverell, New South Wales, providing regional
residential aged care and independent living units. McLean Care
operates 6 residential aged care facilities in Inverell, Guyra, and
Gunnedah in northern New South Wales, and Oakey and Millmerran
in southern Queensland. It also operates co-located independent
living units in Inverell and Gunnedah.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is limited geographic overlap between Respect Group
and McLean Care, with Respect Group’s closest existing
residential aged care facility being located approximately
100 kilometres away by road
b. there are alternative providers of residential aged care and
retirement living services in the regions surrounding McLean
Care’s facilities.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
